newsitem.title: USA: Judge puts preliminary injuction on Norelco ads.
newsitem.headline: Judge puts preliminary injuction on Norelco ads.

text.p: A federal judge ruled in favor of Gillette Co in the first round of the company's court battle with rival Norelco Consumer Products Co.

Judge Reginald Lindsay of the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a preliminary injunction against Norelco's advertisements, which claim that electric shavers cause less irritation then razor blades.

Lindsay ruled the ads must include a "sufficiently conspicuious and contemporaneous statement" that a user of Norelco's Reflex Action electric razors should not expect less irritation until after three weeks.
Gillette claims the Norelco ads are deceptive and has sought punitive and other damages.
"It's gratifying to have the court validate our position that Norelco violated the law and made false and deceptive claims," said Eric Kraus, a spokesman for Gillette.
"We're looking forward to the full trial and expect at that time to convince the court that it's initial order should be expanded and made permanent."
No date has been scheduled for the court date, he said.
In one of the television advertisements, a razor blade spits out fire. In another, the handle of a razor coils like a snake and a forked tongue flicks out between a double-blade.

The radio ads associated the sound of scraping sandpaper and peeling velcro with wet shaving, while the sound of Hallelujah Chorus from Handel's Messiah was associated with Norelco's Reflex Action electric razor.
The ads were the largest in the history of Norelco, a unit of Philips Electronics NV.
